quote: Critics worry that these technologies will be expensive and initially accessible only to the wealthy. If only the rich can afford to edit out genetic diseases or enhance the traits of their children, society could become increasingly stratified. This could lead to a genetic divide where socioeconomic inequalities are literally written into our DNA. In the Australian context, where universal healthcare and the principle of a fair go are deeply cherished, the prospect of a medical advancement that exacerbates inequality is highly troubling. People who hold this view argue that unless we can guarantee equitable access to genome editing, permitting it could undermine the fabric of our egalitarian society.
